display.title: Sefiras HaOmer: Respecting Others and Counting the Days to the Torah
display.summary_short: Why we hold back music during Sefirah and how to respect one another, why Pesach never 'passes over', and why we count the Omer like a prisoner awaiting freedom.
display.summary_long: A set of Sefirah teachings from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, given after Pesach. Uncle Yossi explains that we play no music between Pesach and Shavuos in memory of Rabbi Akiva's students, who died in a plague because they did not respect one another. The lesson for us: never embarrass or insult anyone, give compliments, and encourage a classmate who is working hard, because, as Rabbi Akiva taught, loving your fellow as yourself is a great rule of the Torah. Next, Pesach does not really 'pass over': the matzah gives us faith for the soul and health for the body all year. Finally, he explains the mitzvah of counting the Omer. Like a prisoner who scratches a mark on the wall each day until his release, the Jews who left Egypt counted the days eagerly until they would receive the Torah at Har Sinai, the true freedom of the soul, while the manna made their bodies strong. We too count with excitement toward Shavuos, and toward freedom from golus and from the yetzer hara.
display.lesson: Respect and encourage every friend, and count the days of the Omer eagerly as we prepare to receive the Torah.
